title: Edit Distance
description:
Given two strings word1 and word2, return the minimum number of operations required to convert word1 to word2.

You have the following three operations permitted on a word:

- Insert a character
- Delete a character
- Replace a character

Each operation costs one. Compute the least total cost to transform word1 into word2.

examples.explanation: horse -> rorse (replace 'h' with 'r'), rorse -> rose (remove 'r'), rose -> ros (remove 'e').

intention -> inention (remove 't'), inention -> enention (replace 'i' with 'e'), enention -> exention (replace 'n' with 'x'), exention -> exection (replace 'n' with 'c'), exection -> execution (insert 'u').
Insert a single character to go from the empty string to "a".

constraints: word1 and word2 consist of lowercase English letters.
approach: Let dp[i][j] be the edit distance between the first i characters of word1 and the first j characters of word2. When the current characters match, dp[i][j] inherits the diagonal dp[i-1][j-1]. Otherwise it is one plus the minimum of deletion (dp[i-1][j]), insertion (dp[i][j-1]), and replacement (dp[i-1][j-1]). Base rows/columns are the lengths of the prefixes. Only the previous and current rows are needed, so keeping two rows over the shorter string reduces space. For lengths m and n, time is O(mn) and auxiliary space is O(min(m,n)).
